NPY gene transfer to the rat hippocampus by adeno-associated viral vector serotype 1 (AAV1) or serotype 1–2 (AAV1–2) chimeric vector reduces the severity of seizures induced by intracerebral kainic acid (KA) and kindling epiletopgenesis.
NPY overexpression by AAV vector injection into the dentate gyrus is anticonvulsant, and the chimeric 1/2 serotype is also antiepileptogenic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NPY gene therapy is a promising approach for the treatment of temporal lobe epilepsy.
AAV vectors can deliver a therapeutic transgene into specific brain regions, thereby providing an effective treatment for epilepsy.
NPY overexpression by AAV vector in the dentate hilus is sufficient to reduce kainate seizures by ∼50% and delay their onset.
